newsitem.title: USA: GM to restart car assembly output Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: GM to restart car assembly output Tuesday.

text.p: General Motors Corp said Monday that two car assembly facilities in Oshawa, Ontario that had been idled because of a strike at a parts plant will resume operations with the first shift on Tuesday.
GM said its Buick City car plant in Flint, Mich., and a second car facility in Orion Township, Mich., will re-start production with the second shift on Tuesday.
GM spokesman Tom Klipstine said two car assembly lines in Lansing, Mich., may resume operations sometime Wednesday.
On Sunday, 2,800 United Auto Workers members from Local 909 in Warren, Mich., approved a new contract settlement, ending a strike that began at midnight July 22.

The strike forced GM to idle the six car plants because of a shortage of transmissions and other parts from the Warren powertrain plant. GM said 16,500 hourly workers were affected by the walkout, not including the strikers.
Workers at the Warren plant went back to work at 2300 EDT Sunday.
GM's stock was up 1-3/4 to 58-5/8 in early trading.
